key_insight: ArogyaSutra combines multi-agent reasoning, tool grounding, and dual-memory to improve multilingual medical question answering for Indic languages and multimodal inputs.
clinical_relevance: The framework aims to make AI-assisted medical information more accessible in low-resource Indian language settings where patients may describe symptoms and images in native languages.
method: Built ArogyaBodha, a multilingual multimodal medical QA dataset from 8 sources.
Covers 31 body systems, 6 imaging modalities, and 21 clinical domains across English and 7 Indic languages.
Uses an actor-critic multi-agent design with tool grounding, dual memory, and trajectory distillation.
evidence_signal: Experiments in the abstract report improved multilingual medical reasoning accuracy across all Indic languages, with ablations supporting each component.
watch_item: Performance gains in benchmark settings may not fully translate to real-world clinical use without careful validation, multilingual robustness checks, and safety review.
paper_title: ArogyaSutra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Multimodal Medical Reasoning in Indic Languages
